sanskrit: sacandrakumudaṃ ramyaṃ sārkakāraṇḍavaṃ śubham tiṣyaśravaṇakadambam abhraśaivalaśādvalam
english: The sky, lovely with the moon and water-lilies, auspicious with the sun and ruddy geese, clustered with the Tiṣya and Śravaṇa stars like kadamba blossoms, its meadows of grass like clouds and river-moss —

sanskrit: punarvasu mahāmīnaṃ lohitāṅgamahāgraham airāvatamahādvīpaṃ svātīhaṃsaviloḍitam
english: — with Punarvasu as its great fish, Mars as its great crocodile, the Airāvata constellation as its great island, stirred by the Svātī star and its swans —

sanskrit: vātasaṃghātajātormiṃ candrāṃśuśiśirāmbumat bhujaṃgayakṣagandharvaprabuddhakamalotpalam
english: — its waves born of clashing winds, its waters cooled by the moon's rays, its lotuses and water-lilies awakened among serpents, yakṣas, and gandharvas —

sanskrit: grasamāna ivākāśaṃ tārādhipam ivālikhan harann iva sanakṣatraṃ gaganaṃ sārkamaṇḍalam
english: — as though swallowing the sky, as though painting the lord of stars, as though sweeping away the firmament together with the stellar hosts and the orb of the sun —

sanskrit: mārutasyālayaṃ śrīmān kapir vyomacaro mahān hanūmān meghajālāni vikarṣann iva gacchati
english: the glorious great monkey Hanumān, dweller in wind, traveller through the sky, moved as though dragging apart the masses of clouds — the abode of the wind-god.

sanskrit: pāṇḍurāruṇavarṇāni nīlamāñjiṣṭhakāni ca haritāruṇavarṇāni mahābhrāṇi cakāśire
english: The great clouds gleamed — some pale and reddish, some dark blue and madder-red, others green and orange-hued.

sanskrit: praviśann abhrajālāni niṣkramaṃś ca punaḥ punaḥ pracchannaś ca prakāśaś ca candramā iva lakṣyate
english: Entering into the masses of cloud and emerging again and again, now hidden and now revealed, he appeared like the moon.

sanskrit: nadan nādena mahatā meghasvanamahāsvanaḥ ājagāma mahātejāḥ punar madhyena sāgaram
english: Roaring with a mighty roar whose sound rivalled the thunder of clouds, the great-spirited one came again across the middle of the ocean.

sanskrit: parvatendraṃ sunābhaṃ ca samupaspṛśya vīryavān jyāmukta iva nārāco mahāvego 'bhyupāgataḥ
english: Having touched the lord of mountains Sunābha, the valiant one of great speed approached like a steel arrow loosed from a bowstring.

sanskrit: sa kiṃ cid anusaṃprāptaḥ samālokya mahāgirim mahendrameghasaṃkāśaṃ nanāda haripuṃgavaḥ
english: Having arrived a little way off and beholding the great mountain that resembled Mahendra and a thundercloud, that bull among monkeys let out a roar.

sanskrit: niśamya nadato nādaṃ vānarās te samantataḥ babhūvur utsukāḥ sarve suhṛddarśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Hearing the roar of the roaring one, all those monkeys on every side became eager with longing to behold their companion.

sanskrit: jāmbavān sa hariśreṣṭhaḥ prītisaṃhṛṣṭamānasaḥ upāmantrya harīn sarvān idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Jāmbavān, that foremost of monkeys, his heart thrilled with delight, summoning all the monkeys spoke these words:

sanskrit: sarvathā kṛtakāryo 'sau hanūmān nātra saṃśayaḥ na hy asyākṛtakāryasya nāda evaṃvidho bhavet
english: "In every respect that Hanumān has accomplished his task — there is no doubt of this. For one who had not accomplished his task could not produce a roar of this kind."

sanskrit: tasyā bāhūruvegaṃ ca ninādaṃ ca mahātmanaḥ niśamya harayo hṛṣṭāḥ samutpetus tatas tataḥ
english: Hearing the speed of his arms and thighs and the roar of that great-souled one, the monkeys, overjoyed, leapt up from here and there.

sanskrit: te nagāgrān nagāgrāṇi śikharāc chikharāṇi ca prahṛṣṭāḥ samapadyanta hanūmantaṃ didṛkṣavaḥ
english: Exhilarated, longing to see Hanumān, they moved from treetop to treetop, from peak to peak.

sanskrit: te prītāḥ pādapāgreṣu gṛhya śākhāḥ supuṣpitāḥ vāsāṃsīva prakāśāni samāvidhyanta vānarāḥ
english: Delighted, those monkeys grasped the well-flowering branches at the treetops and waved them about like gleaming garments.

sanskrit: tam abhraghanasaṃkāśam āpatantaṃ mahākapim dṛṣṭvā te vānarāḥ sarve tasthuḥ prāñjalayaḥ tadā
english: Beholding that great monkey descending, resembling a dense mass of cloud, all those monkeys stood with palms joined in reverence.

sanskrit: tatas tu vegavāṃs tasya girer girinibhaḥ kapiḥ nipapāta mahendrasya śikhare pādapākule
english: Then that swift monkey, himself mountain-like, descended upon the tree-covered summit of mount Mahendra.

sanskrit: tatas te prītamanasaḥ sarve vānarapuṃgavāḥ hanūmantaṃ mahātmānaṃ parivāryopatasthire
english: Then all those bulls among monkeys, their hearts full of joy, gathered around and attended upon the great-souled Hanumān.

sanskrit: parivārya ca te sarve parāṃ prītim upāgatāḥ prahṛṣṭavadanāḥ sarve tam arogam upāgatam
english: Surrounding him, they all experienced the highest delight, all with gleaming faces, seeing him returned safe and well.

sanskrit: upāyanāni cādāya mūlāni ca phalāni ca pratyarcayan hariśreṣṭhaṃ harayo mārutātmajam
english: Bringing offerings, roots, and fruits, the monkeys honoured that foremost of monkeys, the son of the wind-god.

sanskrit: vinedur muditāḥ ke cic cakruḥ kila kilāṃ tathā hṛṣṭāḥ pādapaśākhāś ca āninyur vānararṣabhāḥ
english: Some roared with joy, others made the kila-kila cry; exhilarated, those bulls among monkeys brought down branches of trees.

sanskrit: hanūmāṃs tu gurūn vṛddhāñ jāmbavat pramukhāṃs tadā kumāram aṅgadaṃ caiva so 'vandata mahākapiḥ
english: Then Hanumān, that great monkey, reverently saluted his elders and seniors headed by Jāmbavān, and also the prince Aṅgada.

sanskrit: sa tābhyāṃ pūjitaḥ pūjyaḥ kapibhiś ca prasāditaḥ dṛṣṭā devīti vikrāntaḥ saṃkṣepeṇa nyavedayat
english: Honoured by those two, himself worthy of honour, and gratified by the monkeys, that valiant one reported briefly: "The queen has been found."

sanskrit: niṣasāda ca hastena gṛhītvā vālinaḥ sutam ramaṇīye vanoddeśe mahendrasya gires tadā
english: Taking the son of Vālin by the hand, he sat down in a pleasant wooded place on mount Mahendra.

sanskrit: hanūmān abravīd dhṛṣṭas tadā tān vānararṣabhān aśokavanikāsaṃsthā dṛṣṭā sā janakātmajā
english: Then Hanumān, joyful, spoke to those bulls among monkeys: "The daughter of Janaka has been seen — she is dwelling in the Aśoka grove."

sanskrit: rakṣyamāṇā sughorābhī rākṣasībhir aninditā ekaveṇīdharā bālā rāmadarśanalālasā upavāsapariśrāntā malinā jaṭilā kṛśā
english: "Guarded by dreadful rākṣasīs, the blameless young woman, wearing her hair in a single braid, longs to behold Rāma; she is exhausted by fasting, soiled, matted-haired, and emaciated."

sanskrit: tato dṛṣṭeti vacanaṃ mahārtham amṛtopamam niśamya māruteḥ sarve muditā vānarā bhavan
english: Then, hearing that great and nectar-like word "she has been seen" from the son of the wind-god, all the monkeys became joyful.

sanskrit: kṣveḍanty anye nadanty anye garjanty anye mahābalāḥ cakruḥ kila kilām anye pratigarjanti cāpare
english: Some hissed, some roared, some of great strength bellowed; others made the kila-kila cry, and still others roared in response.

sanskrit: ke cid ucchritalāṅgūlāḥ prahṛṣṭāḥ kapikuñjarāḥ añcitāyatadīrghāṇi lāṅgūlāni pravivyadhuḥ
english: Some, those elephant-like monkeys, raised their tails in joy; they curled and waved their long, outstretched tails.

sanskrit: apare tu hanūmantaṃ vānarā vāraṇopamam āplutya giriśṛṅgebhyaḥ saṃspṛśanti sma harṣitāḥ
english: And others, those monkeys elephant-like in might, leapt from the mountain peaks and touched Hanumān with delight.

sanskrit: uktavākyaṃ hanūmantam aṅgadas tu tadābravīt sarveṣāṃ harivīrāḥ madhye vācam anuttamām
english: Then Aṅgada, in the midst of all the monkey heroes, spoke these excellent words to Hanumān who had just finished speaking:

sanskrit: sattve vīrye na te kaś cit samo vānaravidyate yad avaplutya vistīrṇaṃ sāgaraṃ punar āgataḥ
english: "In courage and valour there is no monkey equal to you — you who have leapt across the vast ocean and returned again."

sanskrit: diṣṭyā dṛṣṭā tvayā devī rāmapatnī yaśasvinī diṣṭyā tyakṣyati kākutsthaḥ śokaṃ sītā viyogajam
english: "By good fortune you have seen the queen, the glorious wife of Rāma. By good fortune Kākutstha will abandon the grief born of separation from Sītā."

sanskrit: tato 'ṅgadaṃ hanūmantaṃ jāmbavantaṃ ca vānarāḥ parivārya pramuditā bhejire vipulāḥ śilāḥ
english: Then the monkeys, surrounding Aṅgada, Hanumān, and Jāmbavān, joyful, took their places on the broad rocks.

sanskrit: śrotukāmāḥ samudrasya laṅghanaṃ vānarottamāḥ darśanaṃ cāpi laṅkāyāḥ sītāyā rāvaṇasya ca tasthuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve hanūmad vadanonmukhāḥ
english: Those foremost of monkeys, eager to hear of the crossing of the ocean, the seeing of Laṅkā, of Sītā, and of Rāvaṇa, all stood with palms joined, their faces turned toward Hanumān's countenance.

sanskrit: tasthau tatrāṅgadaḥ śrīmān vānarair bahubhir vṛtaḥ upāsyamāno vibudhair divi devapatir yathā
english: The glorious Aṅgada sat there, surrounded by many monkeys, attended upon like the lord of gods in heaven attended by the celestials.

sanskrit: hanūmatā kīrtimatā yaśasvinā tathāṅgadenāṅgadabaddhabāhunā mudā tadādhyāsitam unnataṃ mahan mahīdharāgraṃ jvalitaṃ śriyābhavat
english: The lofty, great summit of the mountain, occupied with joy by the renowned and illustrious Hanumān and by Aṅgada with Aṅgada's arm clasped about him, blazed with splendour.

sanskrit: tatas tasya gireḥ śṛṅge mahendrasya mahābalāḥ hanumatpramukhāḥ prītiṃ harayo jagmur uttamām
english: Then on the summit of that mountain Mahendra, the mighty monkeys with Hanumān at their head experienced the highest joy.

sanskrit: taṃ tataḥ pratisaṃhṛṣṭaḥ prītimantaṃ mahākapim jāmbavān kāryavṛttāntam apṛcchad anilātmajam
english: Then Jāmbavān, himself overjoyed, questioned that joyful great monkey, the son of the wind-god, about what had transpired in the mission.

sanskrit: kathaṃ dṛṣṭā tvayā devī kathaṃ vā tatra vartate tasyāṃ vā sa kathaṃ vṛttaḥ krūrakarmā daśānanaḥ
english: "How did you see the queen? And how does she fare there? And how has the cruel-actioned Daśānana behaved toward her?"

sanskrit: tattvataḥ sarvam etan naḥ prabrūhi tvaṃ mahākape śrutārthāś cintayiṣyāmo bhūyaḥ kāryaviniścayam
english: "Tell us all of this truthfully, O great monkey. Having heard the matter, we shall deliberate further upon the final determination of the course of action."

sanskrit: yaś cārthas tatra vaktavyo gatair asmābhir ātmavān rakṣitavyaṃ ca yat tatra tad bhavān vyākarotu naḥ
english: "And what is the matter that must be told by us when we go there, and what must be protected there — let your honour explain all that to us."

sanskrit: sa niyuktas tatas tena saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ namasyañ śirasā devyai sītāyai pratyabhāṣata
english: Assigned by him, his body hair standing on end with joy, bowing his head in reverence to the queen Sītā, he replied:

sanskrit: pratyakṣam eva bhavatāṃ mahendrāgrāt kham āplutaḥ udadher dakṣiṇaṃ pāraṃ kāṅkṣamāṇaḥ samāhitaḥ
english: "As you yourselves witnessed, I leapt into the sky from the summit of Mahendra, composed and intent, desiring to reach the southern shore of the ocean.

sanskrit: gacchataś ca hi me ghoraṃ vighnarūpam ivābhavat kāñcanaṃ śikharaṃ divyaṃ paśyāmi sumanoharam
english: "As I was going, something that seemed like a dreadful obstacle appeared: I saw a golden peak, divine and exceedingly lovely,

sanskrit: sthitaṃ panthānam āvṛtya mene vighnaṃ ca taṃ nagam
english: "standing blocking my path — I considered that mountain an obstacle.

sanskrit: upasaṃgamya taṃ divyaṃ kāñcanaṃ nagasattamam kṛtā me manasā buddhir bhettavyo 'yaṃ mayeti ca
english: "Approaching that divine, golden, foremost of mountains, my mind formed the thought: 'I must break through this.'

sanskrit: prahataṃ ca mayā tasya lāṅgūlena mahāgireḥ śikharaṃ sūryasaṃkāśaṃ vyaśīryata sahasradhā
english: "And when struck by my tail, the peak of that great mountain, sun-like in brilliance, was shattered into a thousand fragments.

sanskrit: vyavasāyaṃ ca me buddhvā sa hovāca mahāgiriḥ putreti madhurāṃ bāṇīṃ manaḥprahlādayann iva
english: "And understanding my resolve, that great mountain spoke, as though gladdening my heart, a sweet word: 'Son!'

sanskrit: pitṛvyaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi sakhāyaṃ mātariśvanaḥ mainākam iti vikhyātaṃ nivasantaṃ mahodadhau
english: "'Know me also as your uncle, a friend of Mātariśvan — the one known as Maināka, dwelling in the great ocean.'

sanskrit: pakṣvavantaḥ purā putra babhūvuḥ parvatottamāḥ chandataḥ pṛthivīṃ cerur bādhamānāḥ samantataḥ
english: "'In former times, O son, the foremost mountains had wings and roamed the earth at will, troubling it on all sides.'

sanskrit: śrutvā nagānāṃ caritaṃ mahendraḥ pākaśāsanaḥ ciccheda bhagavān pakṣān vajreṇaiṣāṃ sahasraśaḥ
english: "'Hearing of the conduct of the mountains, the blessed Mahendra, the slayer of Pāka, cut off their wings with his thunderbolt by the thousands.'

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu mokṣitas tasmāt tava pitrā mahātmanā mārutena tadā vatsa prakṣipto 'smi mahārṇave
english: "'But I was saved from that by your father, the great-souled Māruta — at that time, O child, I was hurled into the great ocean.'

sanskrit: rāmasya ca mayā sāhye vartitavyam ariṃdama rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭho mahendrasamavikramaḥ
english: "'And I must render assistance in the cause of Rāma, O subduer of foes — Rāma, the foremost of upholders of dharma, equal in valour to Mahendra.'

sanskrit: etac chrutvā mayā tasya mainākasya mahātmanaḥ kāryam āvedya tu girer uddhataṃ ca mano mama
english: "Hearing this from the great-souled Maināka, having communicated my mission to the mountain, my mind was roused.

sanskrit: tena cāham anujñāto mainākena mahātmanā uttamaṃ javam āsthāya śeṣam adhvānam āsthitaḥ
english: "And being given leave by the great-souled Maināka, adopting my utmost speed, I covered the remaining journey.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ suciraṃ kālaṃ vegenābhyagamaṃ pathi tataḥ paśyāmy ahaṃ devīṃ surasāṃ nāgamātaram
english: "Then for a long time I was advancing rapidly along the path; then I saw the goddess Surasā, mother of serpents.

sanskrit: samudramadhye sā devī vacanaṃ mām abhāṣata mama bhakṣyaḥ pradiṣṭas tvam amārair harisattamam tatas tvāṃ bhakṣayiṣyāmi vihitas tvaṃ cirasya me
english: "That goddess in the midst of the ocean addressed me: 'You, O foremost of monkeys, have been appointed as my prey by the immortals — therefore I shall devour you; you have been ordained for me after a long time.'

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ surasayā prāñjaliḥ praṇataḥ sthitaḥ vivarṇavadano bhūtvā vākyaṃ cedam udīrayam
english: "Addressed thus by Surasā, I stood with palms joined, bowing, and with a changed countenance I spoke these words:

sanskrit: rāmo dāśarathiḥ śrīmān praviṣṭo daṇḍakāvanam lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā sītayā ca paraṃtapaḥ
english: "'The glorious Rāma, son of Daśaratha, the scorcher of foes, has entered the Daṇḍaka forest together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa and with Sītā.'

sanskrit: tasya sītā hṛtā bhāryā rāvaṇena durātmanā tasyāḥ sakāśaṃ dūto 'haṃ gamiṣye rāmaśāsanāt
english: "'His wife Sītā has been abducted by the evil-souled Rāvaṇa — by Rāma's command I shall go to her.'

sanskrit: kartum arhasi rāmasya sāhyaṃ viṣayavāsini
english: "'You who dwell in this domain, you ought to render assistance to Rāma.'

sanskrit: atha vā maithilīṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ cākliṣṭakāriṇam āgamiṣyāmi te vaktraṃ satyaṃ pratiśṛṇoti me
english: "'Or else, having seen Maithilī and Rāma the effortless worker, I shall return into your mouth — I promise you truly.'

sanskrit: evam uktā mayā sā tu surasā kāmarūpiṇī abravīn nātivarteta kaś cid eṣa varo mama
english: "Addressed thus by me, that Surasā, who takes any form at will, declared: 'No one may pass beyond me — this is my boon.'

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ surasayā daśayojanam āyataḥ tato 'rdhaguṇavistāro babhūvāhaṃ kṣaṇena tu
english: "Addressed thus by Surasā, I became ten yojanas in length; and in an instant I became half that measure in breadth.

sanskrit: matpramāṇānurūpaṃ ca vyāditaṃ tanmukhaṃ tayā tad dṛṣṭvā vyāditaṃ tv āsyaṃ hrasvaṃ hy akaravaṃ vapuḥ
english: "And her mouth was opened wide in proportion to my size. Seeing that gaping mouth, I made my body small.

sanskrit: tasmin muhūrte ca punar babhūvāṅguṣṭhasaṃmitaḥ abhipatyāśu tad vaktraṃ nirgato 'haṃ tataḥ kṣaṇāt
english: "And in that moment I became thumb-sized again; swiftly plunging into that mouth, I emerged from it in an instant.

sanskrit: abravīt surasā devī svena rūpeṇa māṃ punaḥ arthasiddhyai hariśreṣṭha gaccha saumya yathāsukham
english: "The goddess Surasā, resuming her own form, said to me again: 'Go, gentle one, O foremost of monkeys, at your ease — may your purpose be accomplished!'

sanskrit: samānaya ca vaidehīṃ rāghaveṇa mahātmanā sukhī bhava mahābāho prītāsmi tava vānara
english: "'And bring together the Vaidehi with the great-souled Rāghava. Be happy, O mighty-armed one — I am pleased with you, monkey.'

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ sādhu sādhvīti sarvabhūtaiḥ praśaṃsitaḥ tato 'ntarikṣaṃ vipulaṃ pluto 'haṃ garuḍo yathā
english: "Then praised by all beings with 'Excellent! Excellent!', I soared up into the vast sky like Garuḍa.

sanskrit: chāyā me nigṛhītā ca na ca paśyāmi kiṃ cana so 'haṃ vigatavegas tu diśo daśa vilokayan na kiṃ cit tatra paśyāmi yena me 'pahṛtā gatiḥ
english: "And my shadow was seized, and I could see nothing. With my speed arrested, looking in all ten directions, I could see nothing there by which my movement had been stolen.

sanskrit: tato me buddhir utpannā kiṃ nāma gamane mama īdṛśo vighna utpanno rūpaṃ yatra na dṛśyate
english: "Then a thought arose in me: why has such an obstacle arisen in my passage — one whose form is not visible?

sanskrit: adho bhāgena me dṛṣṭiḥ śocatā pātitā mayā tato 'drākṣam ahaṃ bhīmāṃ rākṣasīṃ salile śayām
english: "With sorrowing gaze I cast my sight downward, and then I saw a dreadful rākṣasī lying in the water.

sanskrit: prahasya ca mahānādam ukto 'haṃ bhīmayā tayā avasthitam asaṃbhrāntam idaṃ vākyam aśobhanam
english: "Laughing a great laugh, I was addressed by that dreadful one — standing unperturbed she spoke these ungracious words:

sanskrit: kvāsi gantā mahākāya kṣudhitāyā mamepsitaḥ bhakṣaḥ prīṇaya me dehaṃ ciram āhāravarjitam
english: "'Where are you going, O great-bodied one? You are the coveted prey of me who am hungry — satisfy my body long deprived of food.'

sanskrit: bāḍham ity eva tāṃ vāṇīṃ pratyagṛhṇām ahaṃ tataḥ āsya pramāṇād adhikaṃ tasyāḥ kāyam apūrayam
english: "With the word 'Very well!' I accepted her challenge; then I enlarged my body beyond the measure of her mouth.

sanskrit: tasyāś cāsyaṃ mahad bhīmaṃ vardhate mama bhakṣaṇe na ca māṃ sā tu bubudhe mama vā vikṛtaṃ kṛtam
english: "Her great and dreadful mouth grew wide in order to devour me; but she did not perceive me or the transformation I had wrought.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ vipulaṃ rūpaṃ saṃkṣipya nimiṣāntarāt tasyā hṛdayam ādāya prapatāmi nabhastalam
english: "Then in the twinkling of an eye I contracted my vast form and, tearing out her heart, I soared into the sky.

sanskrit: sā visṛṣṭabhujā bhīmā papāta lavaṇāmbhasi mayā parvatasaṃkāśā nikṛttahṛdayā satī
english: "That dreadful one, mountain-sized, her heart wrenched out by me, her arms released, fell into the salt ocean.

sanskrit: śṛṇomi khagatānāṃ ca siddhānāṃ cāraṇaiḥ saha rākṣasī siṃhikā bhīmā kṣipraṃ hanumatā hṛtā
english: "And I heard the sky-going beings and siddhas together with cāraṇas: 'The dreadful rākṣasī Siṃhikā has been swiftly destroyed by Hanumān.'

sanskrit: tāṃ hatvā punar evāhaṃ kṛtyam ātyayikaṃ smaran gatvā ca mahad adhvānaṃ paśyāmi nagamaṇḍitam dakṣiṇaṃ tīram udadher laṅkā yatra ca sā purī
english: "Having slain her and remembering my urgent task, I traversed a great distance and saw the southern shore of the ocean adorned with mountains — where that city of Laṅkā lies.

sanskrit: astaṃ dinakare yāte rakṣasāṃ nilayaṃ purīm praviṣṭo 'ham avijñāto rakṣobhir bhīmavikramaiḥ
english: "When the sun had set, I entered the city, the abode of the rākṣasas, unrecognised by the rākṣasas of dreadful might.

sanskrit: tatrāhaṃ sarvarātraṃ tu vicinvañ janakātmajām rāvaṇāntaḥpuragato na cāpaśyaṃ sumadhyamām
english: "There I searched the entire night for the daughter of Janaka, entering Rāvaṇa's inner apartments, but did not see the slender-waisted one.

sanskrit: tataḥ sītām apaśyaṃs tu rāvaṇasya niveśane śokasāgaram āsādya na pāram upalakṣaye
english: "Then, not seeing Sītā in Rāvaṇa's dwelling, I reached a sea of grief and could discern no farther shore.

sanskrit: śocatā ca mayā dṛṣṭaṃ prākāreṇa samāvṛtam kāñcanena vikṛṣṭena gṛhopavanam uttamam
english: "And while grieving, I saw, enclosed by a wall stretched with gold, an excellent garden adjoining the palace.

sanskrit: sa prākāram avaplutya paśyāmi bahupādapam
english: "Leaping over the wall, I saw it filled with many trees.

sanskrit: aśokavanikāmadhye śiṃśapāpādapo mahān tam āruhya ca paśyāmi kāñcanaṃ kadalī vanam
english: "In the middle of the Aśoka grove stood a great śiṃśapā tree. Climbing it, I saw a golden grove of banana trees.

sanskrit: adūrāc chiṃśapāvṛkṣāt paśyāmi vanavarṇinīm śyāmāṃ kamalapatrākṣīm upavāsakṛśānanām
english: "Not far from the śiṃśapā tree I saw a forest-dweller — dark-complexioned, with lotus-petal eyes, her face emaciated by fasting.

sanskrit: rākṣasībhir virūpābhiḥ krūrābhir abhisaṃvṛtām māṃsaśoṇitabhakṣyābhir vyāghrībhir hariṇīṃ yathā
english: "She was surrounded by misshapen and cruel rākṣasīs who subsist on flesh and blood — like a doe surrounded by tigresses.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśīṃ nārīṃ rāmapatnīm aninditām tatraiva śiṃśapāvṛkṣe paśyann aham avasthitaḥ
english: "Seeing that woman, the blameless wife of Rāma, in such a state, I remained there on that very śiṃśapā tree, watching.

sanskrit: tato halahalāśabdaṃ kāñcīnūpuramiśritam śṛṇomy adhikagambhīraṃ rāvaṇasya niveśane
english: "Then I heard an extremely deep uproar of noise, mingled with the sounds of waist-ornaments and ankle-bells, in Rāvaṇa's dwelling.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ paramodvignaḥ svarūpaṃ pratyasaṃharam ahaṃ ca śiṃśapāvṛkṣe pakṣīva gahane sthitaḥ
english: "Then I, greatly agitated, contracted my form and sat in the śiṃśapā tree like a bird in the dense foliage.

sanskrit: tato rāvaṇadārāś ca rāvaṇaś ca mahābalaḥ taṃ deśaṃ samanuprāptā yatra sītābhavat sthitā
english: "Then Rāvaṇa's wives and the mighty Rāvaṇa himself arrived at that place where Sītā stood.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvātha varārohā sītā rakṣogaṇeśvaram saṃkucyorū stanau pīnau bāhubhyāṃ parirabhya ca
english: "Seeing the lord of the rākṣasa hosts, the shapely Sītā drew her thighs together and clasped her full breasts with her arms.

sanskrit: tām uvāca daśagrīvaḥ sītāṃ paramaduḥkhitām avākśirāḥ prapatito bahu manyasva mām iti
english: "Daśagrīva addressed the deeply sorrowful Sītā, having prostrated with bowed head: 'Think highly of me!'

sanskrit: yadi cet tvaṃ tu māṃ darpān nābhinandasi garvite dvimāsānantaraṃ sīte pāsyāmi rudhiraṃ tava
english: "'If in your pride and arrogance you do not accept me gladly, O Sītā, then after two months I shall drink your blood.'

sanskrit: etac chrutvā vacas tasya rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ uvāca paramakruddhā sītā vacanam uttamam
english: "Hearing those words of the evil-souled Rāvaṇa, Sītā, most wrathful, spoke these excellent words:

sanskrit: rākṣasādhama rāmasya bhāryām amitatejasaḥ ikṣvākukulanāthasya snuṣāṃ daśarathasya ca avācyaṃ vadato jihvā kathaṃ na patitā tava
english: "'O lowest of rākṣasas, how has your tongue not fallen out while speaking unspeakable words to the wife of Rāma of immeasurable splendour, lord of the Ikṣvāku line, and daughter-in-law of Daśaratha?'

sanskrit: kiṃsvid vīryaṃ tavānārya yo māṃ bhartur asaṃnidhau apahṛtyāgataḥ pāpa tenādṛṣṭo mahātmanā
english: "'What indeed is your valour, O ignoble one, O wicked one — you who abducted me in my husband's absence and came here, unseen by that great-souled one?'

sanskrit: na tvaṃ rāmasya sadṛśo dāsye 'py asyā na yujyase yajñīyaṃ satyavāk caiva raṇaślāghī ca rāghavaḥ
english: "'You are not the equal of Rāma — you are not even fit to be his slave, nor mine. The Rāghava is worthy of sacrifice, truthful in speech, and renowned in battle.'

sanskrit: jānakyā paruṣaṃ vākyam evam ukto daśānanaḥ jajvāla sahasā kopāc citāstha iva pāvakaḥ
english: "Addressed thus with harsh words by the daughter of Janaka, Daśānana blazed up suddenly with anger, like fire blazing amid funeral-pyre bones.

sanskrit: vivṛtya nayane krūre muṣṭim udyamya dakṣiṇam maithilīṃ hantum ārabdhaḥ strībhir hāhākṛtaṃ tadā
english: "Rolling his cruel eyes and raising his right fist, he began to strike Maithilī — at which the women cried out in alarm.

sanskrit: strīṇāṃ madhyāt samutpatya tasya bhāryā durātmanaḥ varā mandodarī nāma tayā sa pratiṣedhitaḥ
english: "Leaping out from among the women, that wicked one's foremost wife, named Mandodarī, restrained him.

sanskrit: uktaś ca madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ tayā sa madanārditaḥ sītayā tava kiṃ kāryaṃ mahendrasamavikrama mayā saha ramasvādya madviśiṣṭā na jānakī
english: "And she, tormented by desire, spoke sweet words to him: 'What business do you have with Sītā, O one equal in valour to Mahendra? Sport with me today — Jānakī is not superior to me.'

sanskrit: devagandharvakanyābhir yakṣakanyābhir eva ca sārdhaṃ prabho ramasveha sītayā kiṃ kariṣyasi
english: "'Sport here, my lord, with the daughters of gods and gandharvas, with the daughters of yakṣas as well — what will you do with Sītā?'

sanskrit: tatas tābhiḥ sametābhir nārībhiḥ sa mahābalaḥ utthāpya sahasā nīto bhavanaṃ svaṃ niśācaraḥ
english: "Then that mighty night-wanderer was suddenly lifted up and led to his own palace by those assembled women.

sanskrit: yāte tasmin daśagrīve rākṣasyo vikṛtānanāḥ sītāṃ nirbhartsayām āsur vākyaiḥ krūraiḥ sudāruṇaiḥ
english: "When Daśagrīva had departed, the misshapen-faced rākṣasīs threatened Sītā with cruel and dreadful words.

sanskrit: tṛṇavad bhāṣitaṃ tāsāṃ gaṇayām āsa jānakī tarjitaṃ ca tadā tāsāṃ sītāṃ prāpya nirarthakam
english: "The daughter of Janaka counted their speech as mere straw, and their threats against Sītā were then utterly fruitless.

sanskrit: vṛthāgarjitaniśceṣṭā rākṣasyaḥ piśitāśanāḥ rāvaṇāya śaśaṃsus tāḥ sītāvyavasitaṃ mahat
english: "Their roaring and efforts in vain, those flesh-eating rākṣasīs reported to Rāvaṇa Sītā's great resolve.

sanskrit: tatas tāḥ sahitāḥ sarvā vihatāśā nirudyamāḥ parikṣipya samantāt tāṃ nidrāvaśam upāgatāḥ
english: "Then all of them together, their hopes dashed and their efforts spent, having surrounded her on all sides, fell under the power of sleep.

sanskrit: tāsu caiva prasuptāsu sītā bhartṛhite ratā vilapya karuṇaṃ dīnā praśuśoca suduḥkhitā
english: "And when they had fallen asleep, Sītā, devoted to her husband's welfare, wailing piteously in her misery, grieved deeply, afflicted with sorrow.

sanskrit: tāṃ cāhaṃ tādṛśīṃ dṛṣṭvā sītāyā dāruṇāṃ daśām cintayām āsa viśrānto na ca me nirvṛtaṃ manaḥ
english: "And seeing her in such a state, seeing Sītā's dreadful plight, I rested but my mind found no peace.

sanskrit: saṃbhāṣaṇārthe ca mayā jānakyāś cintito vidhiḥ ikṣvākukulavaṃśas tu tato mama puraskṛtaḥ
english: "And for the purpose of speaking with the daughter of Janaka, I thought about the method; then the lineage of the Ikṣvāku clan was placed by me in the foreground.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu gaditāṃ vācaṃ rājarṣigaṇapūjitām pratyabhāṣata māṃ devī bāṣpaiḥ pihitalocanā
english: "Having heard the speech I spoke, honoured by the company of royal seers, the queen replied to me with eyes brimming with tears.

sanskrit: kas tvaṃ kena kathaṃ ceha prāpto vānarapuṃgava kā ca rāmeṇa te prītis tan me śaṃsitum arhasi
english: "'Who are you? By whom and how have you come here, O bull among monkeys? And what is your bond of affection with Rāma? Please tell me that.'

sanskrit: tasyās tad vacanaṃ śrutvā aham apy abruvaṃ vacaḥ devi rāmasya bhartus te sahāyo bhīmavikramaḥ sugrīvo nāma vikrānto vānarendo mahābalaḥ
english: "Hearing those words of hers, I too spoke words: 'O queen, your husband Rāma has an ally of dreadful valour — the heroic king of monkeys of great might, named Sugrīva.'

sanskrit: tasya māṃ viddhi bhṛtyaṃ tvaṃ hanūmantam ihāgatam bhartrāhaṃ prahitas tubhyaṃ rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā
english: "'Know me as his servant Hanumān, come here — I have been sent to you by your husband, Rāma the effortless worker.'

sanskrit: idaṃ ca puruṣavyāghraḥ śrīmān dāśarathiḥ svayam aṅgulīyam abhijñānam adāt tubhyaṃ yaśasvinī
english: "'And this — the glorious Rāma, that tiger among men, son of Daśaratha, has himself given this ring as a token of recognition to you, O illustrious one.'

sanskrit: tad icchāmi tvayājñaptaṃ devi kiṃ karavāṇy aham rāmalakṣmaṇayoḥ pārśvaṃ nayāmi tvāṃ kim uttaram
english: "'That being so, I wish to be instructed by you, O queen — what shall I do? Shall I carry you to the side of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa? Or is there some other resolution?'

sanskrit: etac chrutvā viditvā ca sītā janakanandinī āha rāvaṇam utsādya rāghavo māṃ nayatv iti
english: "Hearing and understanding this, Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, said: 'Let the Rāghava come and, having vanquished Rāvaṇa, take me away.'

sanskrit: praṇamya śirasā devīm aham āryām aninditām rāghavasya manohlādam abhijñānam ayāciṣam
english: "Bowing my head in reverence to the noble, blameless queen, I asked for a token of recognition to delight Rāma's heart.

sanskrit: evam uktā varārohā maṇipravaram uttamam prāyacchat paramodvignā vācā māṃ saṃdideśa ha
english: "Addressed thus, the shapely one, most greatly agitated, gave me the foremost, excellent jewel, and instructed me in words.

sanskrit: tatas tasyai praṇamyāhaṃ rājaputryai samāhitaḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ parikrāmam ihābhyudgatamānasaḥ
english: "Then, bowing reverently to that princess, composed in mind, I performed a clockwise circumambulation, my heart set on returning here.

sanskrit: uttaraṃ punar evāha niścitya manasā tadā hanūman mama vṛttāntaṃ vaktum arhasi rāghave
english: "She spoke again a further word, having resolved upon it in her mind: 'Hanumān, you must relate my situation to the Rāghava.'

sanskrit: yathā śrutvaiva nacirāt tāv ubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau sugrīvasahitau vīrāv upeyātāṃ tathā kuru
english: "'Act in such a way that those two heroes, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, together with Sugrīva, come here speedily upon hearing.'

sanskrit: yady anyathā bhaved etad dvau māsau jīvitaṃ mama na māṃ drakṣyati kākutstho mriye sāham anāthavat
english: "'If this should be otherwise, my life shall be but two months. Kākutstha will not see me — I shall die here like one without a protector.'

sanskrit: tac chrutvā karuṇaṃ vākyaṃ krodho mām abhyavartata uttaraṃ ca mayā dṛṣṭaṃ kāryaśeṣam anantaram
english: "Hearing that pitiful speech, anger overtook me, and I looked upon the remaining task that must be done next.

sanskrit: tato 'vardhata me kāyas tadā parvatasaṃnibhaḥ yuddhakāṅkṣī vanaṃ tac ca vināśayitum ārabhe
english: "Then my body grew, becoming like a mountain; eager for battle, I began to destroy that grove.

sanskrit: tad bhagnaṃ vanaṣaṇḍaṃ tu bhrāntatrastamṛgadvijam pratibuddhā nirīkṣante rākṣasyo vikṛtānanāḥ
english: "When the grove was broken and the animals and birds were confused and frightened, the misshapen-faced rākṣasīs woke up and looked about.

sanskrit: māṃ ca dṛṣṭvā vane tasmin samāgamya tatas tataḥ tāḥ samabhyāgatāḥ kṣipraṃ rāvaṇāyācacakṣire
english: "And seeing me in that grove, gathering together from here and there, they quickly went to Rāvaṇa and reported.

sanskrit: rājan vanam idaṃ durgaṃ tava bhagnaṃ durātmanā vānareṇa hy avijñāya tava vīryaṃ mahābala
english: "'O king, this formidable grove of yours has been destroyed by that wicked monkey, not knowing your valour, O mighty one.'

sanskrit: durbuddhes tasya rājendra tava vipriyakāriṇaḥ vadham ājñāpaya kṣipraṃ yathāsau vilayaṃ vrajet
english: "'O lord of kings, command quickly the slaying of that evildoer of wicked intellect who has acted against your pleasure, so that he may come to destruction.'

sanskrit: tac chrutvā rākṣasendreṇa visṛṣṭā bhṛśadurjayāḥ rākṣasāḥ kiṃkarā nāma rāvaṇasya mano'nugāḥ
english: "Hearing this, the lord of rākṣasas dispatched the rākṣasas called the Kiṃkaras, exceedingly difficult to overcome, who follow Rāvaṇa's will.

sanskrit: teṣām aśītisāhasraṃ śūlamudgarapāṇinām mayā tasmin vanoddeśe parigheṇa niṣūditam
english: "Eighty thousand of them, bearing spears and clubs in their hands, were slain by me in that wooded place with a mace.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu hataśeṣā ye te gatā laghuvikramāḥ nihataṃ ca mayā sainyaṃ rāvaṇāyācacakṣire
english: "Those remaining survivors among them, swift in their movement, went and reported to Rāvaṇa the army I had slain.

sanskrit: tato me buddhir utpannā caityaprāsādam ākramam
english: "Then a thought arose in me and I ascended the caitya tower.

sanskrit: tatrasthān rākṣasān hatvā śataṃ stambhena vai punaḥ lalāma bhūto laṅkāyā mayā vidhvaṃsito ruṣā
english: "And having slain a hundred rākṣasas there with a pillar, I, who had become the ornament of Laṅkā, destroyed it in anger.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahastasya sutaṃ jambumālinam ādiśat
english: "Then he dispatched Jambumālin, the son of Prahasta.

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ balasaṃpannaṃ rākṣasaṃ raṇakovidam parigheṇātighoreṇa sūdayāmi sahānugam
english: "That rākṣasa, powerful and skilled in battle, together with his followers I slew with an exceedingly dreadful mace.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā rākṣasendras tu mantriputrān mahābalān padātibalasaṃpannān preṣayām āsa rāvaṇaḥ parigheṇaiva tān sarvān nayāmi yamasādanam
english: "Hearing this, the lord of rākṣasas Rāvaṇa sent the minister's sons, of great might, equipped with infantry forces — I sent all of them to Yama's abode with the very same mace.

sanskrit: mantriputrān hatāñ śrutvā samare laghuvikramān pañcasenāgragāñ śūrān preṣayām āsa rāvaṇaḥ tān ahaṃ saha sainyān vai sarvān evābhyasūdayam
english: "Hearing that the minister's sons, swift in battle, had been slain, Rāvaṇa sent five generals of armies, warriors — all of them together with their armies I slew entirely.

sanskrit: tataḥ punar daśagrīvaḥ putram akṣaṃ mahābalam bahubhī rākasaiḥ sārdhaṃ preṣayām āsa saṃyuge
english: "Then again Daśagrīva sent his son Akṣa of great might together with many rākṣasas into battle.

sanskrit: taṃ tu mandodarī putraṃ kumāraṃ raṇapaṇḍitam sahasā khaṃ samutkrāntaṃ pādayoś ca gṛhītavān carmāsinaṃ śataguṇaṃ bhrāmayitvā vyapeṣayam
english: "But that prince, son of Mandodarī, skilled in battle, who suddenly leapt into the sky — I seized him by the feet and, whirling him around a hundredfold together with his shield and sword, I crushed him.

sanskrit: tam akṣam āgataṃ bhagnaṃ niśamya sa daśānanaḥ tata indrajitaṃ nāma dvitīyaṃ rāvaṇaḥ sutam vyādideśa susaṃkruddho balinaṃ yuddhadurmadam
english: "Hearing that Akṣa had come and been destroyed, Daśānana Rāvaṇa, most furious, directed his second son named Indrajit, the mighty one, wild with battle-frenzy.

sanskrit: tasyāpy ahaṃ balaṃ sarvaṃ taṃ ca rākṣasapuṃgavam naṣṭaujasaṃ raṇe kṛtvā paraṃ harṣam upāgamam
english: "His entire army and he himself, that bull among rākṣasas — having rendered them powerless in battle, I experienced supreme joy.

sanskrit: mahatā hi mahābāhuḥ pratyayena mahābalaḥ preṣito rāvaṇenaiṣa saha vīrair madotkaṭaiḥ
english: "For it was with great confidence that this mighty-armed, mighty one had been sent by Rāvaṇa with heroes intoxicated with pride.

sanskrit: brāhmeṇāstreṇa sa tu māṃ prabadhnāc cātivegataḥ rajjūbhir abhibadhnanti tato māṃ tatra rākṣasāḥ
english: "But he bound me with a Brāhma weapon with great speed; then the rākṣasas there bound me with ropes.

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya samīpaṃ ca gṛhītvā mām upānayan dṛṣṭvā saṃbhāṣitaś cāhaṃ rāvaṇena durātmanā
english: "And taking hold of me, they led me to the presence of Rāvaṇa; being seen, I was addressed by the evil-souled Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭaś ca laṅkāgamanaṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca tad vadham tat sarvaṃ ca mayā tatra sītārtham iti jalpitam
english: "And questioned about my coming to Laṅkā and the slaying of those rākṣasas, I declared all of it there: 'It was for the sake of Sītā.'

sanskrit: asyāhaṃ darśanākāṅkṣī prāptas tvadbhavanaṃ vibho mārutasyaurasaḥ putro vānaro hanumān aham
english: "'Desirous of seeing her, I came to your abode, O lord — I am the monkey Hanumān, the direct son of Māruta.'

sanskrit: rāmadūtaṃ ca māṃ viddhi sugrīvasacivaṃ kapim so 'haṃ dautyena rāmasya tvatsamīpam ihāgataḥ
english: "'Know me as Rāma's messenger, a monkey, the minister of Sugrīva — I have come here to your presence on Rāma's embassy.'

sanskrit: śṛṇu cāpi samādeśaṃ yad ahaṃ prabravīmi te rākṣaseśa harīśas tvāṃ vākyam āha samāhitam dharmārthakāmasahitaṃ hitaṃ pathyam ivāśanam
english: "'And hear also the message I convey to you — the lord of monkeys speaks to you, O lord of rākṣasas, a composed word, wholesome in dharma, artha, and kāma, beneficial as beneficial food.'

sanskrit: vasato ṛṣyamūke me parvate vipuladrume trea rāghavo raṇavikrānto mitratvaṃ samupāgataḥ
english: "'While I was dwelling on mount Ṛṣyamūka abounding in trees, Rāma the warrior, valiant in battle, came to friendship with me.'

sanskrit: tena me kathitaṃ rājan bhāryā me rakṣasā hṛtā tatra sāhāyyahetor me samayaṃ kartum arhasi
english: "'He told me, O king: My wife has been abducted by a rākṣasa — for that reason you should make a compact with me for assistance.'

sanskrit: vālinā hṛtarājyena sugrīveṇa saha prabhuḥ cakre 'gnisākṣikaṃ sakyaṃ rāghavaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
english: "'The Rāghava along with Lakṣmaṇa made a fire-witnessed alliance of friendship with Sugrīva who had been deprived of his kingdom by Vālin.'

sanskrit: tena vālinam utsādya śareṇaikena saṃyuge vānarāṇāṃ mahārājaḥ kṛtaḥ saṃplavatāṃ prabhuḥ
english: "'By him, having felled Vālin in battle with a single arrow, Sugrīva was made the great king of monkeys, lord of those who leap.'

sanskrit: tasya sāhāyyam asmābhiḥ kāryaṃ sarvātmanā tv iha tena prasthāpitas tubhyaṃ samīpam iha dharmataḥ
english: "'His assistance must be rendered by us here with our entire being — by him I have been sent rightfully to your presence here.'

sanskrit: kṣipram ānīyatāṃ sītā dīyatāṃ rāghavasya ca yāvan na harayo vīrā vidhamanti balaṃ tava
english: "'Let Sītā be brought swiftly and given to the Rāghava, before the heroic monkeys scatter your forces.'

sanskrit: vānarāṇāṃ prabhavo hi na kena viditaḥ purā devatānāṃ sakāśaṃ ca ye gacchanti nimantritāḥ
english: "'For the origin of the monkeys has not been known to anyone before — they are those who go to the presence of the gods when invited.'

sanskrit: iti vānararājas tvām āhety abhihito mayā mām aikṣata tato ruṣṭaś cakṣuṣā pradahann iva
english: "'Thus the king of monkeys speaks to you' — so I addressed him. Then he looked at me with a burning gaze, enraged, as though setting me on fire.

sanskrit: tena vadhyo 'ham ājñapto rakṣasā raudrakarmaṇā
english: "By that rākṣasa of dreadful deeds I was condemned to death.

sanskrit: tato vibhīṣaṇo nāma tasya bhrātā mahāmatiḥ tena rākṣasarājo 'sau yācito mama kāraṇāt
english: "Then his brother, named Vibhīṣaṇa, of great wisdom, petitioned that king of rākṣasas on my account.

sanskrit: dūtavadhyā na dṛṣṭā hi rājaśāstreṣu rākṣasa dūtena veditavyaṃ ca yathārthaṃ hitavādinā
english: "'The killing of a messenger is not found in the treatises on kingship, O rākṣasa; and a messenger must speak truly, as a well-wisher.'

sanskrit: sumahaty aparādhe 'pi dūtasyātulavikramaḥ virūpakaraṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ na vadho 'stīha śāstrataḥ
english: "'Even in the case of a very great offence by a messenger, O one of incomparable might, mutilation is found — but not killing — according to the treatises.'

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇenaivam ukto rāvaṇaḥ saṃdideśa tān rākṣasān etad evādya lāṅgūlaṃ dahyatām iti
english: "Addressed thus by Vibhīṣaṇa, Rāvaṇa commanded those rākṣasas: 'Let this tail of his be set on fire today.'

sanskrit: tatas tasya vacaḥ śrutvā mama pucchaṃ samantataḥ veṣṭitaṃ śaṇavalkaiś ca paṭaiḥ kārpāsakais tathā
english: "Then, hearing his word, my tail was wrapped all around with hemp bark and cotton cloth.

sanskrit: rākṣasāḥ siddhasaṃnāhās tatas te caṇḍavikramāḥ tad ādīpyanta me pucchaṃ hanantaḥ kāṣṭhamuṣṭibhiḥ
english: "Then those rākṣasas, ready-armed, of fierce valour, set my tail alight, striking it with wooden clubs.

sanskrit: baddhasya bahubhiḥ pāśair yantritasya ca rākṣasaiḥ na me pīḍā bhavet kā cid didṛkṣor nagarīṃ divā
english: "Bound as I was with many nooses and controlled by the rākṣasas, I felt no pain whatsoever — I who desired to see the city in daylight.

sanskrit: tatas te rākṣasāḥ śūrā baddhaṃ mām agnisaṃvṛtam aghoṣayan rājamārge nagaradvāram āgatāḥ
english: "Then those heroic rākṣasas, making loud proclamation, led me bound, enveloped in fire, along the royal road to the city gate.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ sumahad rūpaṃ saṃkṣipya punar ātmanaḥ vimocayitvā taṃ bandhaṃ prakṛtiṣṭhaḥ sthitaḥ punaḥ
english: "Then I contracted my very large body once more, freed myself from that bondage, and stood restored to my natural state.

sanskrit: āyasaṃ parighaṃ gṛhya tāni rakṣāṃsy asūdayam tatas tan nagaradvāraṃ vegenāplutavān aham
english: "Seizing an iron club, I slew those guards; then I leapt swiftly to that city gate.

sanskrit: pucchena ca pradīptena tāṃ purīṃ sāṭṭagopurām dahāmy aham asaṃbhrānto yugāntāgnir iva prajāḥ
english: "And with my blazing tail, unperturbed, I burned that city with its towers and gateways, like the fire at the end of an age burning living beings.

sanskrit: dagdhvā laṅkāṃ punaś caiva śaṅkā mām abhyavartata dahatā ca mayā laṅkāṃ dagdhā sītā na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Having burned Laṅkā, again a fear overtook me: while burning Laṅkā, surely Sītā too has been burned — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: athāhaṃ vācam aśrauṣaṃ cāraṇānāṃ śubhākṣarām jānakī na ca dagdheti vismayodantabhāṣiṇām
english: "Then I heard the auspicious speech of the cāraṇas who spoke a wondrous message: 'Jānakī has not been burned.'

sanskrit: tato me buddhir utpannā śrutvā tām adbhutāṃ giram punar dṛṣṭā ca vaidehī visṛṣṭaś ca tayā punaḥ
english: "Then a thought arose in me after hearing that wondrous speech; the Vaidehi was seen again and I was sent off again by her.

sanskrit: rāghavasya prabhāvena bhavatāṃ caiva tejasā sugrīvasya ca kāryārthaṃ mayā sarvam anuṣṭhitam
english: "By the power of the Rāghava, and by your splendour, and for the purpose of Sugrīva's mission, all has been accomplished by me.

sanskrit: etat sarvaṃ mayā tatra yathāvad upapāditam atra yan na kṛtaṃ śeṣaṃ tat sarvaṃ kriyatām iti
english: "All of this has been duly accomplished by me there — whatever remaining task has not been done here, let all of that now be carried out."

sanskrit: etad ākhyānaṃ tat sarvaṃ hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ bhūyaḥ samupacakrāma vacanaṃ vaktum uttaram
english: Having narrated all of that account, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, proceeded to speak a further word:

sanskrit: saphalo rāghavodyogaḥ sugrīvasya ca saṃbhramaḥ śīlam āsādya sītāyā mama ca plavanaṃ mahat
english: "The effort of the Rāghava is fruitful, and the diligence of Sugrīva, having encountered the character of Sītā — as is my great leap.

sanskrit: āryāyāḥ sadṛśaṃ śīlaṃ sītāyāḥ plavagarṣabhāḥ tapasā dhārayel lokān kruddhā vā nirdahed api
english: "The character of the noble Sītā is worthy of her, O bulls among leapers — by her ascetic power she could sustain the worlds, or if angered she could burn them utterly.

sanskrit: sarvathātipravṛddho 'sau rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ yasya tāṃ spṛśato gātraṃ tapasā na vināśitam
english: "In every respect that Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, has grown excessively powerful — the body of one who has touched her has not been destroyed by her ascetic power.

sanskrit: na tad agniśikhā kuryāt saṃspṛṣṭā pāṇinā satī janakasyātmajā kuryād utkrodhakaluṣīkṛtā
english: "What a flame of fire touched by hand could not do, the daughter of Janaka, stirred to the turbulence of extreme anger, could do.

sanskrit: aśokavanikāmadhye rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ adhastāc chiṃśapāvṛkṣe sādhvī karuṇam āsthitā
english: "In the middle of the Aśoka grove of the evil-souled Rāvaṇa, beneath the śiṃśapā tree, the virtuous one sits in pitiable condition.

sanskrit: rākṣasībhiḥ parivṛtā śokasaṃtāpakarśitā meghalekhāparivṛtā candralekheva niṣprabhā
english: "Surrounded by rākṣasīs, wasted by grief and anguish, she is like a crescent of the moon surrounded by streaks of cloud — shorn of its lustre.

sanskrit: acintayantī vaidehī rāvaṇaṃ baladarpitam pativratā ca suśroṇī avaṣṭabdhā ca jānakī
english: "The Vaidehi gives no thought to Rāvaṇa who is arrogant with strength; she is devoted to her husband, lovely-hipped, and firm in resolve — Jānakī.

sanskrit: anuraktā hi vaidehī rāmaṃ sarvātmanā śubhā ananyacittā rāme ca paulomīva puraṃdare
english: "For the auspicious Vaidehi is devoted to Rāma with her entire being, her mind fixed on Rāma alone — like Paulomī fixed upon Purandara.

sanskrit: tad ekavāsaḥsaṃvītā rajodhvastā tathaiva ca śokasaṃtāpadīnāṅgī sītā bhartṛhite ratā
english: "Clothed in a single garment, covered with dust as well, her limbs wasted by grief and anguish, Sītā is devoted to her husband's welfare.

sanskrit: sā mayā rākṣasī madhye tarjyamānā muhur muhuḥ rākṣasībhir virūpābhir dṛṣṭā hi pramadā vane
english: "She was seen by me in the forest, that lady in the midst of rākṣasīs, threatened again and again by the misshapen rākṣasīs.

sanskrit: ekaveṇīdharā dīnā bhartṛcintāparāyaṇā adhaḥśayyā vivarṇāṅgī padminīva himāgame
english: "Wearing her hair in a single braid, wretched, her every thought absorbed in her husband, sleeping on the ground, her limbs pale — like a lotus pool at the onset of winter.

sanskrit: rāvaṇād vinivṛttārthā martavyakṛtaniścayā kathaṃ cin mṛgaśāvākṣī viśvāsam upapāditā
english: "She who had turned away from Rāvaṇa's purpose and had resolved to die — that doe-eyed one was somehow brought to trust.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃbhāṣitā caiva sarvam arthaṃ ca darśitā rāmasugrīvasakhyaṃ ca śrutvā prītim upāgatā
english: "Then she was spoken to and all the matter was revealed to her; and upon hearing of the friendship of Rāma and Sugrīva, she experienced joy.

sanskrit: niyataḥ samudācāro bhaktir bhartari cottamā
english: "Her conduct is regulated and her devotion to her husband is supreme.

sanskrit: yan na hanti daśagrīvaṃ sa mahātmā daśānanaḥ nimittamātraṃ rāmas tu vadhe tasya bhaviṣyati
english: "That the great-souled Daśānana does not slay Daśagrīva — Rāma shall be merely the instrument in his slaying.

sanskrit: evam āste mahābhāgā sītā śokaparāyaṇā yad atra pratikartavyaṃ tat sarvam upapādyatām
english: "Thus does the greatly blessed Sītā dwell, absorbed in grief — whatever should be done about this, let all of that now be brought to fruition."
